row.evidence: dbt's pricing page lists 'SSO, Role-Based Access Control, and SCIM provisioning' under Enterprise (Custom pricing), and the SCIM docs say 'You must be on an Enterprise or Enterprise+ plan.'
row.notes: Status unchanged (gated). The June 'Team' plan is now called Starter, still $100 per user/month (the page does not say whether that is annual or monthly). June's '$300+/u/mo' Enterprise price and 3x multiplier have no first-party source and were dropped; Enterprise is Custom pricing. SCIM requires Okta or Entra ID connected as the SSO provider (both set up as custom apps against the generic SCIM 2.0 base URL); other IdPs are pointed at the dbt APIs. SCIM license mapping (dbtLabs extension licenseType) is Okta-only. SCIM DELETE removes the user's license. Administrative API is on Starter and above; audit log (UI and API) is Enterprise.

plans.name: Starter
plans.notes: Billing period not stated on the pricing page.

scim.notes: Base URL is shown in Account settings > SSO & SCIM; path from the API spec and rate-limit page; host varies by region/cell (e.g. {account_prefix}.us1.dbt.com).

auth.token_source: Account settings > SSO & SCIM > Enable SCIM > Create SCIM token

deprovision.notes: Okta/Entra deactivate via the active attribute. A SCIM DELETE 'will remove the users license from the account'; deleting a developer-licensed user opens up their seat. Whether deactivation alone frees the seat is not stated.

custom.how: urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:dbtLabs:2.0:User with licenseType (developer, read_only, analyst, it); SCIM license mapping is Okta-only.

roles.how: Licenses via the dbtLabs SCIM extension licenseType (Okta only) or SSO group-to-license mapping (Entra); permission sets are assigned to SCIM-synced groups in dbt, not by SCIM.

rate_limits.text: 20 requests every 5 seconds per account for SCIM user create (POST) and replace (PUT); other SCIM calls are outside that limit. 429 with Retry-After and x-rate-limit-retry-after-seconds.

limitations.text: SCIM works only when Okta or Entra ID is the connected SSO provider, and SSO and SCIM should use the same IdP.
SCIM license mapping is Okta-only; Entra uses SSO group-to-license mapping.
SCIM does not assign permission sets; they must be added to SCIM-synced groups in dbt.
With SCIM enabled, manual invites, user edits and group membership changes are disabled by default.
Entra cannot import existing dbt users or groups; Entra provisioning IPs rotate and conflict with IP restrictions.
New SCIM users with no existing account are invited by email and are not licensed until they accept, which can break group pushes.

capabilities.notes: Users join via invites; no non-SCIM user delete or deactivate endpoint was seen in the v2/v3 specs.

endpoints.purpose: Assign permission sets to a group
Request a bulk audit log export
Download a bulk audit log export

webhooks_user_events.notes: Webhooks cover dbt job events only.

rate_limits.text: Administrative API: 5,000 requests per minute per account; over the limit returns 429 with a five-minute cooldown.

okta.notes: dbt's guide has admins create a custom SAML 2.0 app in Okta and enable SCIM on it; no OIN catalogue page was found (okta.com/integrations/dbt-cloud, /dbt-labs and /dbt returned 404).

open_questions: Pricing page does not say whether Starter's $100 per user/month is annual or monthly billing.
Whether SCIM deactivation (active=false) frees the developer seat, and whether it ends sessions, is not documented.
SCIM filtering and pagination parameters are not documented in the API spec.
SCIM token expiry is not documented (docs only advise rotation).
No Okta OIN, Entra gallery, Google, OneLogin or JumpCloud catalogue app found; SCIM docs only support Okta and Entra.
No non-SCIM endpoint to delete or deactivate a user was found in the v2/v3 specs.
Enterprise price and seat minimum are not public.
